rules.title: Strong indicative systems
rules.rule: The present singular uses -e, -st, -ð and plural -að, subject to stated stem/dental changes. Preterite first/third singular share the selected singular stem; second singular uses the plural stem with -e; all plural persons use -on. Ādrīfan has ī/ā/i; gehātan retains ge- and selects hā-/hēt-, with hǣt- in second/third present singular. Flēon is contracted: flēo-, flīeh-, flēah-, flug- are explicitly distributed, not mechanically generated from the citation.

rules.title: Weak I selected systems
rules.rule: Gemētan and grētan retain ē; t before the third-singular dental yields selected -tt, and the preterite is -tte/-ttest/-tton. Ēhtan has ēht in third present singular and ēhte/-est/-on in the preterite, not an invented doubled dental. Cȳðan selects cȳst and cȳð after regular dental interaction; cȳðde/-dest/-don is selected, with attested cȳdde variants recognized. These are complete present/preterite indicative systems only.

rules.title: Weak II selected systems
rules.rule: Geopenian and leornian have -ie, -ast, -að, -iað in the present, and -ode, -odest, -ode, -odon in the preterite. The plural form serves all persons; each person/number coordinate is still displayed.

rules.title: Āgan positive indicative
rules.rule: Āh/āhst/āh and plural āgon form the present; āhte/āhtest/āhte and plural āhton form the preterite. These cells are the full defined positive indicative. Supplied nāh does not establish a negative paradigm.

rules.title: Nine complete direct-command pairs
rules.rule: Both singular and plural are provided for sęndan, bringan, ādrīfan, flēon, gemētan, geopenian, weorpan, leornian and rīsan. Strong long stems and long weak I stems use the selected bare singular; contracted flēon has flēoh; weak II uses -a singular and -iað plural. The commands do not imply newly productive subjunctives.

rules.title: Five complete base pairs with unequal learning scope
rules.rule: Gewyrcean/gewyrcende/geworht, gierwan/gierwende/gierwed and sęttan/sęttende/sętt have productive present and past bases; their larger syntactic uses remain separately bounded. Gewītan/gewītende/gewiten and sittan/sittende/seten are recognition/reference pairs. A displayed participle base is not a complete adjectival declension or an unrestricted perfect/progressive system.

rules.title: Two complete plain/inflected shape pairs
rules.rule: Ādrīfan/ādrīfanne and genēosian/genēosianne show both shapes. Plain infinitives are productive only with the already taught specified modals; inflected shapes are recognition/reference.

rules.title: Twelve construction positions, not twelve inflectional cells
rules.rule: The complete present and preterite habban construction display has six person/number positions for each tense and binds prior finite auxiliary forms, prior accusative ðæt hūs and new productive geworht. Count these as construction examples separately; do not fabricate multiword lexical forms. The finite auxiliary agrees with the subject; the object is the participle patient.
Complete defined ādrīfan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative person or group expelled; previously taught fram+dative may identify the source of departure.

rules.rule: Complete defined gehātan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative thing promised and optionally dative recipient. No general promise-clause or calling/commanding sense is inferred.

rules.rule: Complete defined flēon present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Intransitive flight, or accusative person/thing avoided. This verb is distinct from flēogan, fly.

rules.rule: Complete defined gemētan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative person or thing found. The preterite gemētte is not the past participle gemētt.

rules.rule: Complete defined geopenian present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative thing opened, including mouth or eyes; no reflexive/intransitive system is silently established.

rules.rule: Complete defined grētan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative person greeted or taken leave of, extended explicitly to the native-land object required in Cook21.12. Weak grētan is distinct from the strong homonym meaning weep.

rules.rule: Complete defined cȳðan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative thing announced or a ðæt content clause; optionally dative recipient. Selected cȳst follows regular dental loss before -st, cȳð the coalescence of two dentals. Past cȳdde is an attested alternative to selected cȳðde.

rules.rule: Complete defined ēhtan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Selected accusative person pursued/persecuted, directly evidenced in Matthew 10.23. Genitive government is also attested and may be accepted if its forms are supported.

rules.rule: Complete defined āgan present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative possession. This is the positive present/preterite indicative only; no imperative, subjunctive, nonfinite or negative system is implied.

rules.rule: Complete defined leornian present/preterite indicative system.
rules.scope_and_limits: Accusative thing learned when expressed; æt+dative identifies the person from whom one learns. Objectless learn from me is independently evidenced.

Interpret narrative temporal relations from context, clause relations and lexical meaning.
rules.scope_and_limits: The two inflected tenses do not map one-to-one to modern English simple/progressive/perfect categories; prior present-for-future remains in force.

rules.rule: A simple preterite can express action earlier than another past viewpoint.
rules.scope_and_limits: Relative anteriority can be made explicit in translation without inventing an Old English compound form.

rules.rule: Finite habban with a selected transitive past participle expresses a completed action or present/past result.
rules.scope_and_limits: The auxiliary agrees with the subject, while the accusative object is the patient of the participle. Selected bare participles are productive. Object-agreeing alternatives are recognized/accepted only within independently supported inflection; no arbitrary causative or intransitive have-perfect is introduced.

rules.rule: Recognize wesan with an intransitive past participle, specifically gewiten.
rules.scope_and_limits: The subject is the departing participant; the phrase is not passive merely because it contains be. Recognize the contextual completed-departure meaning; no unrestricted productive system.

rules.rule: Recognize wesan with a present participle, specifically sittende.
rules.scope_and_limits: Context may motivate simple, progressive or durative English. A simple finite Old English verb may also receive progressive English. No obligatory modern progressive category is inferred.

rules.rule: Compare an active transitive clause with a supported agentless passive and distinguish event from resulting state.
rules.scope_and_limits: Retains prior u07-passive: a passive subject is the affected entity; converting to agentless passive omits any named active agent. Wearð may focus on coming into the condition, wæs on a state or contextually an event. No mechanical became/was rule or fram-agent production.

rules.rule: Express simultaneous, anterior and intended-later time relative to a reporting viewpoint.
rules.scope_and_limits: Prior report subjunctives provide simultaneous sīe/wǣre; anterior hæfde plus selected participle is new. Hæfde is syncretic and context identifies the report function. Wolde plus infinitive retains volition/intention and does not guarantee later realization. Indicative reports may be defensible; no automatic backshift or subjunctive=false.

rules.rule: Intransitive cease/fail without an expressed genitive object, including seedtime and harvest ceasing or failing in Cook19.16. Earlier genitive cessation remains available for ceasing from rule.
Accusative person killed; distinguishes this lethal sense from previously taught strike/smite.
Seeing is asserted absolutely in the bounded temporal clauses of Cook20.2; no accusative object must be invented.
On+dative with rich/lowly predicates; not physical motion into the noun.
Beforan+dative marks the person before whom someone is sent; extends earlier static location explicitly.
Accusative thing prepared; with the selected past participle, habban retains that accusative patient.
Accusative text or letter written; prior morphology does not itself establish this lexical frame.
Accusative person/thing sent and dative recipient; beforan+dative is a separate ahead-of frame.
Accusative thing thrown, including the assigned hook.
Welig on+dative identifies the thing or resource in which a person, place or productive event is rich; includes harvest rich in fruit.
Ābūtan+accusative, surrounding a person/thing or building around it.
Selected accusative after sending among a group; the directly attested sheep/wolves passage supports this precise use. Dative location is also attested but is not the selected productive frame.
Æt+dative marks the person from whom one learns, as in leornian æt a person.
For+dative identifies the beneficiary in the assigned payment/giving expression; not every for-case or causal use.
Accusative quantity of time expresses duration.
rules.scope_and_limits: The supplied forty-years phrase is explicitly local support; this does not establish all numeral systems.

rules.rule: A numeral plus genitive measure noun can state breadth or height.
rules.scope_and_limits: The measure noun fōt is separately taught in full; the twenty-feet quantity remains supplied local support.

rules.rule: Nǣfre and preverbal ne reinforce one negative meaning.
rules.scope_and_limits: Bounded never/never again constructions only; nǣfre mā means never more/again. Do not teach a general negative-pronoun family by implication.

rules.rule: Predicative genitive identifies a possessor; predicative possessive adjectives agree with what is possessed.
rules.scope_and_limits: Distinguish an owner in genitive from ðīn in the gender/number of dæg or niht. Earlier attributive forms are reused with an explicit new syntax milestone.

rules.rule: Quantitative predicative mā means more in number with a plural subject.
rules.scope_and_limits: Selected indeclinable mā plus prior ðonne comparison standard; distinct from earlier adverbial amount of doing. No new māran comparative-adjective system is required.

rules.rule: On+accusative with adjectival ōðer may have an understood city noun.
rules.scope_and_limits: Supplied local on ōðre [ceastre] analysis, using the actual prior ceaster system; no unrestricted nominal ellipsis production is inferred.

rules.rule: Two separated swā tokens express equality of degree.
rules.scope_and_limits: First swā is degree; second swā introduces the standard. Bind each to the actual prior swa-invariant form and its new sense; do not invent a compound form spanning the intervening adjective.

rules.rule: Swā plus a nominal compares the persons sent to sheep.
rules.scope_and_limits: Explicit bounded extension beyond the prior finite comparative clause.

rules.rule: Recognize the selected past reported condition and possibility in the Picts and Scots passage.
rules.scope_and_limits: Source-specific gif ... gefultumoden and ðæt ... meahten are supplied/analyzed in context. This does not promote a complete new conditional or modal subjunctive system.

rules.rule: Finding accusative rest may include the dative beneficiaries.
rules.scope_and_limits: Declared application of Cook160–161 general dative-of-benefit syntax to the bounded Cook21.9 requirement; not a separately quoted dictionary valency witness. It does not require a preposition translating English unto.

rules.rule: Supplied nāh for the negative possession clause in Cook20.4.
rules.scope_and_limits: Reuse already supplied nis for the other local negative clause; full negative systems are not production.

principle: Complete morphology and productive syntax are distinct assignments. Prior learning is established by the actual baseline records, not by headword familiarity or archived course milestones.
